mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate directly increases the discount rate for equity valuation, reducing the present value of future cash flows and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship is continuous and holds across all monetary regimes without threshold requirements.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is negative in more than 50% of 3-year rolling windows, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is positive in the majority of periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% and remains elevated for at least one month, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a trigger is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days. The effect is multiplicative, not additive, as both indicators must deteriorate together.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of instances where both series decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by a cumulative FEDFUNDS increase of more than 0.25% over the last three months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increased by >0.25% in last 3 months
evidence_refs: doc:Monetary Policy Tightening and Equity Returns
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods meeting the tightening cycle trigger, or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A stronger labor market, indicated by a rising employment level (PAYEMS), increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This relationship is continuous and holds across all labor market conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 5-day S&P 500 returns is negative in more than 50% of 3-year rolling windows, or the correlation between PAYEMS and 5-day returns is negative in the majority of periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a trigger is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad economic slowdown driven by supply constraints and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The effect is multiplicative, as both indicators must deteriorate together to trigger the signal.
failure_condition: The interaction term (INDPRO * HOUST) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of instances where both series decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a high-unemployment regime that weakens consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a trigger is below 0.03.
